subsystems.holistic:
This slice is the product's reading room — the dossier tabs, the library cards, the compendium, and the DM's composer — and it is, on the whole, mature work that takes its own constitution seriously. The premium seam is held with genuine discipline: FaithSection's three-mode gate (ACTIVE/TEASER/HIDDEN) is enforced by construction (faithPanelModel never reads config.latentPantheon), WarFaithTab composes the gated FaithSection and resolves worldState only through the deliberately light war read-models, RumorsTab implements the includeGroundTruth reveal exactly per convention, and every deity surface (DeityAssignmentPanel, EventComposerDeityField, PantheonActivationStrip) gates FIRST and stays name-free below the gate. Dormancy is equally consistent: SteadingsSection, RealmStrip, LivingWorldSignalRow, HealthPip, the M6d flow section, and market prices all render literally nothing for a pre-wave world, with the reasoning written into headers. The W-COMPOSER-2 composer is the slice's architectural high point — a thin orchestrator over pure buildEvent, a manifest-driven navigator where unavailability teaches instead of hiding, the staleness-key law making preview≡apply hold by construction, and refusals surfaced as prose.

The failures are at the seams, and they cluster in the newest code. The worst is the mutable docket's edit lane: editSeed.js is a hand-maintained reverse of buildEvent with zero test coverage, and it already disagrees with its forward twin — a queued cult REMOVAL reopens as an imposition (the remove sentinel is snapshot-null with a non-null ref, which editSeed misreads as assign) and a custom stressor loses its isCustom flag and authored label on re-stage. This is the owner's most-bitten class — a write that survives one path and ghosts another — landed the same day the docket shipped. The second cluster is the analytics/privacy floor: two surfaces pass raw user data (Supabase userId; free-typed search text) as event props, bypassing the hashUserId floor and contradicting the event dictionary that declares both events prop-less. Third, single-source-of-truth erosion at display edges: the default-on magazine Summary reads prosperity as an object where the engine emits a string (its prosperity+stressors block has never rendered), and DailyLife still computes food deficit from the gross engine number the A+ pdf.3 fix banished everywhere else — an in-dossier contradiction on import-dependent settlements.

As product surface, the slice is unusually legible: cause-chains-as-sentences, empty states written as invitations, refusals that teach, and the counterpart criterion visibly honored (every dossier fact the composer can now force). The nit list (dead icon ternary, stray parens, empty occupier titles) is short for 17.6k LOC. Grade A-: the constitution holds everywhere I traced it, but the two high findings are real trust breakers in exactly the surfaces (paid conversion, the DM's queued intent) where trust is the product.
strengths: The premium/reveal seam is enforced BY CONSTRUCTION, not by caller discipline: faithPanelModel cannot name a latent deity because it never reads config.latentPantheon; every deity control gates before any name renders; RumorsTab is a textbook includeGroundTruth implementation.

Dormancy/additivity is uniform across the new-wave surfaces (SteadingsSection, RealmStrip, LivingWorldSignalRow, flow/market sections): absent state renders literally nothing, and the headers explain the byte-identical contract.

EventComposer V2 is excellent architecture: pure buildEvent assembly, manifest-driven verb availability with grayed-with-reason teaching, the staleness-key making preview→apply identity hold by construction, veto refusals rendered as in-world prose, and the LAPSED derivation on queued intentions.

Cross-surface read-model reuse is real, not aspirational: library pips consume the same warStatus/deriveSystemState models the dossier uses (livingWorldSignals header documents it), and food/prosperity displays cite the one-fact-one-source law with the PDF.

Legibility as a design law reaches the user: cause chains as sentences (FaithSection), empty states as invitations, defensive raw-id guards (LivingWorldSignalRow safeName), and honest disabled states with reasons everywhere.
A11y house patterns are consistently applied where extracted (WAI-ARIA tabs with roving tabIndex in both tab strips, dialog focus trap in DossierLadderModal, progressbar semantics on SaveQuotaMeter).

findings.title: WelcomeCreditCard ships the raw Supabase userId as an analytics prop, bypassing the hashUserId privacy floor
findings.evidence: `Funnel.track(EVENTS.WELCOME_CREDIT_GRANTED, { userId })` (and :113 `WELCOME_CREDIT_SPENT, { userId }`). track()'s 2nd arg is props — docs say 'coarse properties only (no PII)'; only opts.userId is hashed (analytics.js:127-128). Both events are essential-class, so sendToProvider mirrors the RAW id to the third-party provider; enqueueEvent stores it first-party.
findings.why: Direct violation of the privacy-first analytics doctrine (id-free enrichment) and of analytics.js's own hashing floor, on the paid-conversion event pair; docs/analytics-event-dictionary.md declares both events prop-less.
findings.fix_shape: Change both calls to `Funnel.track(EVENT, {}, { userId })` (the signupCompleted pattern) so the id rides the hashed opts lane; add a structural test that no Funnel.track call site passes userId/user_id inside props (grep-based source scan, the repo's established prevention idiom).
findings.deferral_checked: docs/COMPREHENSIVE_REVIEW_2026-07-13.md (no welcome-credit finding), docs/DESIGN_ANALYTICS_V2.md, docs/analytics-event-dictionary.md (declares props '—'), usage-telemetry memory (id-free doctrine). Not recorded anywhere.

findings.title: Mutable-docket edit silently inverts a queued IMPOSE_CULT removal into an imposition (editSeed↔buildEvent asymmetry)
findings.evidence: `if (p.deityRef != null) fields.deityRef = ...; if (p.deityRef == null) fields.deityMode = 'remove'` — but an IMPOSE_CULT removal's payload is {deityRef: <cultRef>, snapshot: null} (mutateEntities.js:877-890), so deityMode stays 'assign'. reconcileCultImposition returns 'replaced'/'refresh' for a same-ref probe (cultImpositionApply.js:88), so canStageDeityEvent passes; buildEvent's assign branch resolves a snapshot and updateQueuedEvent (campaignSlice.js:773) replaces the queued removal in place.
findings.why: The DM edits a queued 'remove cult X' (even just its description), clicks Apply, and the docket now holds 'impose cult X' — while the UI select shows the placeholder because the seeded deityRef is filtered out of addOptions. Silent intent inversion in the owner-law surface ('each queued commit is editable') shipped with W-COMPOSER-2; editSeed has zero test coverage (no test imports eventToComposerIntent).
findings.fix_shape: In editSeed, key the remove detection per type: IMPOSE_CULT remove = `p.snapshot == null` → seed deityMode:'remove' + cultRemoveRef:p.deityRef (add cultRemoveRef to applyComposerIntent's setters map). Then add the missing structural guard: a round-trip pin test asserting buildEvent(applyComposerIntent(eventToComposerIntent(e))) reproduces every queued payload byte-for-byte across all authorable verbs — the whole reverse-map class is untested.
findings.deferral_checked: docs/DESIGN_EVENT_COMPOSER_V2.md §10 (mutable docket law — no editSeed caveat), W-COMPOSER-2 memory deferrals (budget red/FP-G7 only), editSeed.js in-file notes (only the derived-values non-seeding is recorded as deliberate). Not deferred.

subsystems.holistic:
This slice is the product's storefront — auth, pricing, checkout, the account console, the public gallery, and the shell that carries the dossier — and most of it now reads like deliberately engineered commerce infrastructure rather than accreted UI. The round-1 fix program visibly landed: config/tierFacts.js is a genuinely excellent piece of structural prevention (every tier fact derived once from the pricing catalog, pinned to the enforcement gate AND walked across six surfaces by a contract test with forbidden-literal regexes), the owner-ruled $2.99 export flip is enforced through one shared decision table (resolveExportAccess) consumed identically by BuyThisDossier and SettlementDetail with defense-in-depth re-checks inside the export runner, shareMap now forwards the full publish_map param bag through one serializer documented as the security boundary, and the founder seat count flows from a single FOUNDER_SEAT_CAP through the live RPC meter. The anon reveal seam is handled with real care: PublicDossierView → OutputContainer threads playerView/shareDm/publicDossier through explicit tab gates with written rationale per gate, per-NPC visibility stores only deltas against the settlement default, the chronicle's public projection is disclosed in the share flow's own copy, and the admin console is least-privilege throughout (masked emails, reveal-requires-audited-reason, soft-delete-first). The landing fixture — frozen real engine output with a replayable seed and a written regen policy — is the kind of honesty-as-marketing detail few products bother with.

Against that strong baseline, the two high findings matter precisely because they sit on the funnel's narrowest points. AuthModal — the primary sign-in surface — closes itself when the user presses Enter to submit or types a space in a password, because the inner card lacks the one-line keydown propagation guard every sibling modal carries; a failed sign-in error can never be seen. And the wizard's save flow never writes save identity back into the store, so the owner-ruled free-tier commerce ladder (save first → buy the $2.99 durable right) dead-ends on the generate surface while duplicate save clicks silently consume the free tier's three slots and the exit dialog gaslights the user about an unsaved draft. Both are small fixes; both are the exact class (state written on one path, ghosted on another; half-applied pattern adoption) this codebase's own doctrine warns about.

The medium finding continues the honesty theme the program itself established: the post-purchase success page — read seconds after a customer pays — promises the free tier an editing capability the shipped gate denies, and restates tier facts as literals on surfaces the tierFacts walker doesn't cover. The ratchet exists; it just needs its walk list extended to every conversion surface, including ones minted after F4.

The residue is small and known: five round-1 lows (corrupted HowToUse prose on the thesis-closing marketing page, the never-written terrain key on the gallery hero, Dialog's off-stack Escape handling, five dead-but-tested primitives) were found, verified, and then fell between the wave plans and the dead-code disposition ledger — dropped threads, not decisions. As code, the slice is unusually literate (comments explain why, cite findings and rulings, and record seams), consistently accessible, and disciplined about lazy-loading against the first-paint ratchet. As product surface, it is one AuthModal guard and one saveId stamp away from A− territory; the underlying architecture already deserves it.

subsystems.holistic:
This slice is the connective tissue of the product — 15 Zustand sub-slices sharing one Immer store, a durable persistence outbox, the multi-tick advance session, and the undo/snapshot machinery — and it reads as genuinely mature production code. The round-1 fix program demonstrably landed and held: the M10b lastLivingAdvanceAt cursor is stamped inside BOTH Phase-2 commit paths (advance at campaignAdvanceSession.js:312, resume at :511, each with an explanation of why it must live inside the atomic persist); the pendingEdits COMMITTABLE_EDIT_KINDS no-silent-drop contract is enforced at the queue mouth and kept in lockstep with the dispatcher; resetSettlementIdentity is a real single chokepoint that all four load paths route through; the persist envelope now has version/migrate plus a deep-merge that backfills new DEFAULT_CONFIG keys; and the store-2 advance-in-flight guards cover the queue/cancel/docket/status mutators with typed no-op reasons that map to plain-language toast copy. The operation manifest + exempt ledger with a completeness walker is exemplary structural prevention, and the outbox (supersede-dedup, per-key serialization gates, bounded backoff, crash-durable mirror, barrier ops) is a carefully reasoned piece of infrastructure.

The findings are therefore residual edges of classes that are already 90% closed — but they are real, and two are the owner's most-bitten shape. First, the typed-refusal contract stops one layer short of the user: queueSettlementEvent's {queued:false} refusal rides through applyEvent looking like success, and the EventComposer resets the form and even raises the stale-narrative modal for an order that never queued — a silent intent drop with success-shaped UX, live for the whole duration of a parked pause. Second, the outbox's ordering guarantee is keyed on the exact partial-key set while call sites write overlapping columns under different kinds (and aiSlice bypasses the outbox entirely for ai_data), so the "same columns serialize" premise is violated by the code's own callers. Third, the worldpulse-core-1 pause-window fix covered proposals/party/docket but missed rules edits and spatial canonize — both still ghost on resume, with no UI gate either. Alongside these: resolveRegionalImpact missed the guard its sibling got, town renames never reach the row name column, addToCampaign strands queued intentions that the drain then destroys silently, useMapBridge documents a placement gate that does not exist in mapSlice, and useCampaignAutoResume reads a store field nothing ever writes.

Round-1 lows that were never scheduled (store-7 authSignIn resolveTier, store-8 sign-out view residue, state-lifecycle-8 deleteCampaign's orphaned pulse-undo snapshots) remain open as recorded; they are not re-reported here. As product surface, the slice's typed-reason discipline (ADVANCE_ERROR_TEXT), the while-you-were-away digest, and the visible queue-refusal news show the legibility doctrine reaching the state layer; the gap is that a few refusal shapes still die before reaching the eye. Constitution compliance is strong: dormancy (pausedAdvance absent-when-clear, byte-neutral clears), the premium seam at store call sites with tier-blind domain, virtual reads for legacy saves, and deliberate lazy-body splits protecting the first-paint ratchet are all consistently executed and consistently documented in-line.

findings.title: Clock-bound queue refusal rides through applyEvent as success — composer resets the form and drops the DM's order silently during in-flight/parked advances
findings.evidence: applyEvent: `const queued = state.queueSettlementEvent(activeSaveId, event); if (queued) { ...return queued; }` — queueSettlementEvent returns a TRUTHY refusal `{ queued:false, reason:'advance_in_flight'|'advance_paused' }` (campaignSlice.js:694,700). EventComposer.jsx:391-405 only branches on `entry.veto`; a refusal falls through to `resetAfterApply()` and `if (entry && !entry.queued && narrated) setStaleNotice(...)`.
findings.why: During a parked pause (which lasts until the DM resolves majors — potentially a whole session) any event composed on a clock-bound settlement is silently discarded while the UI resets the form and raises the stale-narrative modal: a paying DM's intent drop with success-shaped UX. applyEventBatch likewise counts refusals as successful logEntries.
findings.fix_shape: Make applyEvent wrap the refusal in an ok:false ActionResult with userMessage from ADVANCE_ERROR_TEXT; EventComposer branches on `entry.queued === false` (keep the form, toast the reason); applyEventBatch classifies queued:false entries as refusals. Add a composer-during-pause store test beside advancePauseResume.test.js.
findings.deferral_checked: Not in playbook §0.0.2, round-1 register (store-2 covered the guard itself, whose comment explicitly says 'the UI can toast the reason' — no UI does), or in-file seam notes.

findings.title: Outbox ordering guarantee is keyed on exact partial-key sets while call sites write overlapping columns under different kinds — stale-blob resurrection race
findings.evidence: kindForPartial: 'writes to the same columns... a version-history-only write and a settlement write coexist (they touch different columns)'. But live kinds all writing the `data` column include 'campaignState+settlement' (applyEvent), 'settlement+timestamp' (applyMapEdit), 'campaignState+settlement+timestamp' (destroy), 'campaignState+settlement+versionHistory' (revert), 'aiData+campaignState+settlement' (applyEvent+narrative). supabaseUpdate has no `timestamp` column at all.
findings.why: Different kinds never share a serialization gate, so a backing-off older op (e.g. a map edit) can land AFTER a newer applyEvent write and revert the settlement column in the cloud; reload then resurrects the undone state — the exact ghost-write class. aiSlice compounds it by writing ai_data via direct savesService.update, bypassing the outbox while applyEvent's op also carries aiData.
findings.fix_shape: Key the per-op gate on the mapped COLUMN set (strip non-column keys like timestamp), or serialize all same-saveId ops whose column sets intersect; route aiSlice's ai_data writes through persistSaveUpdate so one lane owns the column. Add an interleaved-kinds outbox test.
findings.deferral_checked: outbox.js/campaignSliceShared.js headers assert the guarantee (no recorded caveat); not in §0.0.2, round-1 register, or DEAD_CODE_DISPOSITION.

findings.title: Town rename never persists the row `name` column — renamed settlements revert their display name after reload on every row-name surface
findings.evidence: persist = `{ settlement: cloneJson(nextSettlement), ...(isCanon ? { campaignState..., timestamp } : {}) }` — no `name` key, though supabaseUpdate maps `partial.name` and supabaseList/listMeta return `name: row.name`. Repo-wide grep: no persistSaveUpdate call ever carries `name`. CampaignFolder.jsx:26 reads `match?.name` first.

findings.title: addToCampaign strands the moved settlement's queued intentions in the old campaign, where the drain silently destroys them
findings.evidence: addToCampaign strips the settlement from every other campaign's settlementIds but never touches their worldState.pendingEvents; removeFromCampaign explicitly drops them ('otherwise they'd be silently destroyed at the next tick'). drainQueuedEvents.js:88 `if (!save || !save.settlement) continue;` — no refusal — then the drain clears pendingEvents wholesale.
findings.why: Re-homing a settlement (single or via useLibraryBulkSelect.addToCampaignBulk) leaves its queued orders in campaign A; A's next advance vaporizes them with no refusal news — violating the W-COMPOSER-2 §10 'refused VISIBLY, never silently dropped' law and the mutable-docket promise.
findings.fix_shape: In addToCampaign, apply removeFromCampaign's pendingEvents drop (or migrate entries to the target campaign) for every campaign the settlement leaves; additionally make the drain emit a 'not_member' refusal instead of `continue`.
findings.deferral_checked: removeFromCampaign's own comment proves the class was known and fixed on one path only; no deferral for the add/move path in §0.0.2 or the register.

findings.title: useMapBridge documents addPlacement as 'the authoritative gate' returning {ok,reason} — but mapSlice.addPlacement has no gate and returns undefined; the bridge path places ungated
findings.evidence: 'addPlacement is the authoritative gate (campaign / canon / no-duplicate)... rejected here without mutating' then `if (res && res.ok === false) showToast(...)`. mapSlice.addPlacement (mapSlice.js:284-335) unconditionally writes the placement and returns nothing; WorldMap.jsx:108 passes the raw store action.
findings.why: A settlementPlaced bridge event that bypasses handleDrop's pre-checks (direct FMG placement, re-entrant echo) mutates placements with no campaign/canon/duplicate check; PLACEMENT_REJECT_COPY is dead code and the documented refusal toast can never fire — the backstop the hook promises does not exist.
findings.fix_shape: Implement the typed gate in mapSlice.addPlacement (return {ok:false, reason:'no-campaign'|'not-canon'|'duplicate'} using the same checks handleDrop performs) so both entry points share one authoritative gate; the hook's consumer code already expects that shape.
findings.deferral_checked: Round-1 components-dossier-1 covered the image-mode drop contract, not this bridge-event gate; no deferral note in mapSlice, useMapBridge, or §0.0.2.

findings.title: useCampaignAutoResume reads store field lastActiveCampaignId that nothing ever writes — the 'resume last-used campaign' behavior is dead
findings.evidence: `const lastActiveCampaignId = useStore(s => s.lastActiveCampaignId);` — repo-wide grep finds zero writers and no slice declares the field; partialize wouldn't persist it anyway. Doc claims 'this reopens the campaign the user last used'.
findings.why: The selector is always undefined, so auto-resume silently always picks activeCampaigns[0] (most-recently-updated) — correct-ish by coincidence but divergent from the documented contract, and a trap for anyone extending resume behavior.
findings.fix_shape: Stamp lastActiveCampaignId in setActiveCampaign and persist it (localStorage alongside the campaign cache, keyed by owner), or delete the dead branch and fix the doc to say most-recently-updated.
findings.deferral_checked: Not in DEAD_CODE_DISPOSITION.md, §0.0.2, or the round-1 register; no in-file seam note.

findings.title: initOutbox on App mount re-runs loadMirror, wiping the live op queue and in-flight gates that earlier child effects may already have populated
findings.evidence: outbox.js module-load already primes via loadMirror(); App.jsx:190 calls initOutbox() in an effect, and loadMirror() resets `_ops = []; _inflightByKey = new Map()`. Child-component effects (auto-resume catch-up persist, loadCampaigns) run before the parent App effect and can enqueue/attempt ops first.
findings.why: An op inflight at that instant loses its serialization gate and its queue entry while the mirror (which normalized it to 'queued') is replayed by drainReady — a duplicate concurrent write to the same row, breaking the ordering guarantee in a narrow boot window.
findings.fix_shape: Make loadMirror merge into a non-empty in-memory queue (or no-op when _ops is non-empty and gates exist), or run initOutbox at store-module init instead of an App effect.
findings.deferral_checked: No note in outbox.js/initOutbox headers, §0.0.2, or the register; the module-load prime comment suggests the double-load was seen but the reset interaction is unaddressed.

subsystems.holistic:
This slice is the strongest client-infrastructure layer I have reviewed at this scale of solo-built product, and it has visibly improved since round 1 (A-). The round-1 fix program landed here for real: exportThumb now exists end-to-end (mapBridge typed api, sf-bridge handler, harness tests); the entity-ref renderer trio is ported and wired (ProseParagraph/ProseText import the tokenizer); tierFacts.js gives tier truth one derived home pinned to the enforcement gate by a contract walker; the analytics queue was split into an eager-leaf/lazy-applier pair with a consent purge keyed on payload presence (lib-infra-2), a cross-pinned snapshot cap (lib-infra-3), sessionId + corpus stamping (lib-infra-5), and a force-drain that removes the old wedge-forever path; the campaign PDF now consumes the living-world read models (lib-infra-7); F41 moved PDF rendering into a worker with a principled feature-detected fallback. I checked each of these against the round-1 register and found no regressions.

The engineering culture on display is rare: nearly every module carries a header explaining not just what it does but which failure mode it exists to prevent, which budget it defends, and which test pins it. First-paint discipline is a pervasive convention (dynamic-import normalize in saves/accountImport, one-importer-per-lazy-module to avoid chunk-manifest leaks in spatialUsage, footer-only copy import in App.jsx). The commerce chain — checkoutReconcile's verify-then-poll state machine, the keyed pendingDossier stash with paid-immunity and LRU-on-unpaid-only, the retro-claim voucher with terminal/transient distinction — reasons about every strand of the anonymous-buyer lifecycle in-file. campaignSync's tombstone + pendingSync deletion-resurrection policy is a textbook treatment of the owner's most-bitten bug class. Privacy is defended by construction (structuralFingerprint copies known-good paths and a test scans output for fixture secrets; spatialUsage emits counts never keys; importScrub is the single writer for the dormancy strip). Deliberate deferrals are recorded where they will be found (the listMeta DISPOSITION comment is exemplary).

The one substantive round-2 gap is simulation-adjacent: the usage-telemetry side-channel froze at rev 7 while roughly seven mover waves merged behind it, so the adoption lens — the module's stated reason to exist — cannot see naval transit, pestilence, disinformation/credibility, upswing arcs, resource dynamics, or momentum. That is a whitelist-without-walker problem, the exact shape structural-prevention exists for, and it will silently understate the new engine's reach in every real campaign until extended. The remainder of the findings are recorded round-1 lows that no F-wave carried plus a small fresh copy-truth drift on the dormant email surface; none threaten correctness of money, persistence, or the constitution. Constitution compliance is clean throughout this slice: telemetry is a read-only side-channel with goldens explicitly out of reach, the premium seam is respected (gallery reveal flags are owner-opt-in, imports strip seeds and pantheons), and nothing here feeds the party back into fit math. Grade A rather than A+ because the telemetry coverage gap undermines a stated product purpose and the recorded-lows backlog needs one sweep commit to clear.
strengths: Analytics transport architecture: eager-leaf/lazy-applier split (analyticsQueue/analyticsFlush) with an acyclic shared-state module, consent purge keyed on payload presence, synthetic/dogfood/production corpus stamping, and a force-drain that provably cannot wedge — privacy-first telemetry at production grade

Commerce trust chain: checkoutReconcile's honest SUCCESS/PROCESSING/FAILED state machine, keyed pendingDossier stash that never TTL-purges a paid artifact, and the retro-claim voucher lifecycle with terminal-vs-transient clearing — every failure mode reasoned about in-file

First-paint discipline as a lived convention, not a rule: dynamic-import of the 30kB normalize closure, one-importer-per-lazy-module to avoid chunk-manifest byte leaks, footer-only copy import in the shell, all annotated with the enforcing test
campaignSync deletion-resurrection policy (tombstones + pendingSync marker + TTL reconcile + server-owned access fields) — a model answer to the owner's most-bitten lifecycle class

Defense-in-depth sanitization with single writers: importScrub as the one dormancy strip both import paths share, allowlist-by-construction structural fingerprints scanned by test, chronicle allowlist re-applied client-side, DOMPurify with forced-safe anchors
F4's tierFacts module: tier claims derived once from the pricing catalog and pinned to the enforcement gate by a contract walker that also forbids raw literals on conversion surfaces
Self-documenting deferral culture — the saves.listMeta DISPOSITION comment ('deferred F42 INFRA, not dead code to re-find') is exactly how a deferral should be recorded

subsystems.holistic:
The data tables are the best-governed layer I have reviewed in this codebase, and the round-1 fix program visibly landed here: the 33-key resource-classification pin is exemplary (hand-checked EXPECTED table, coverage test that forces a human decision on every new resource, synthetic boundary probes for the barley/ley and charcoal/coal substring classes — I traced all 33 keys through the current regexes and each lands on its pinned row, so the taxonomy chip is confirmed live on this branch); the services join is now exact-name-first with anti-shadow invariants pinned; the civic-government institutions have dedicated service menus; the five newer stressors reached stressInstitutionEffects and historyData's tension vocabulary whole; the fishing dedup landed with its own joins pin; and the catalog grew real identity machinery (kernel slugify, module-load collision check, id-first joins with the legacy fuzzy behavior frozen byte-compatibly). The in-file fix-annotation culture — corrective comments naming round-1 finding ids at every touched row — makes the tables auditable in a way few data layers are.

Against that strong baseline, round 2 finds four things the register should carry. First, a fresh high: customRegistry's prebuilt trade-goods enumeration ingests IMPORT_GOODS_BY_TIER as if it were name-keyed like GOODS_MODIFIERS_BY_TIER, but it is group-keyed — so the registry mints phantom goods named "basic"/"fromHigher"/"fromCityOrMetropolis"/"fromHinterland"/"fromMetropolis" as refIds while every real import good is absent; the anomalous bare "Enslaved persons" key is the only import good that ingests correctly, which is itself the tell that the row was authored to fit the broken reader. Second, a fix-wave regression: G2's terrain-boost rename pass created double-stacking modifier rows (forest lists Sawmill twice at 3× and 2.5×; mountain and hills list both "Quarry" and "Stone quarry", which both substring-match the single Stone quarry institution). Third, a false lifecycle claim: the fishing-dedup comment promises the retired 'fish' chain id is "kept (below) for persisted-save resolution," but no keeper exists anywhere in src — and the W-DISCOVERY surgical reconcile provably can never prune a persisted stale chain, so pre-fix saves keep the duplicate industry until a full regen. Fourth, coal_deposits still ships the stray 'timber' commodity; the classifier now guards against it, but commodity-level consumers (deriveLocalCommodities) still count coal settlements as timber producers while the COMMODITY_CATEGORY_MAP's own 'coal'/'peat' rows sit unreachable.

The unfixed round-1 tail is real but honest: NPC_ROLES remains a 12,252-byte byte-identical dead duplicate with misnamed siblings (never dispositioned — DEAD_CODE_DISPOSITION scoped itself to orphaned modules), the slavic suffix pool still carries its 8/30 duplicates, seven supplyChainData processors still resolve to nothing, and the nit batch (dup tags, popToTier contradiction, stale headers, Mossgate "lakeside") is verbatim where round 1 left it. None regressed; none were formally deferred either, which is the process gap — findings that are neither fixed nor written down as deferred get re-found, exactly as here.

As simulation substance, the tables compose well: the two-axis category governance, the tag vocabulary with its orphan ratchet, and the chain/resource/terrain join pins mean the id-first world the constitution wants is mostly built here. Grade B+ rather than A-: the fresh registry-contract break reaches a product surface, one regression came from the fix wave itself, and a documented-but-false persistence claim is the owner's most-bitten bug class wearing a reassuring comment.
strengths: The 33-key resource-classification pin (tests/domain/resourceTaxonomyClassification.test.js): hand-checked EXPECTED table, coverage test forcing human sign-off on any new resource, synthetic boundary probes for the exact substring classes that bit (barley/ley, charcoal/coal, shore/ore) — all 33 keys hand-traced through the current regexes match their pinned rows

Catalog identity machinery (institutionalCatalog.js:2354-2405): kernel slugify, module-load collision check with a rename-or-die error, exact normalized lookup, and id-first joins whose id-sets are built FROM the legacy fuzzy matcher so behavior is frozen byte-compatibly with known false matches documented rather than silently changed

Dense joins-test estate (29 files in tests/joins) pinning services key resolution + anti-shadow invariants, goods exact-name keys, chain-id validity, resourceChains display-name resolution, and the fishing dedup — structural prevention is embedded in the data contracts, not bolted on

Vocabulary governance: categoryVocabulary.js documents the deliberately-independent dual classification axes with the reasoning inline; entityTags.js carries an orphan-tag ratchet with the COMMUNICATION-removal precedent recorded in-file

First-paint leaf discipline: resourceChains, supplyChainResourceIndex, npcTraitWeights, finishedGoodsCategory, stressTypesMeta all split with @enforced-by annotations pointing at the byte-budget ratchet and explicit do-not-re-export warnings

Fix-annotation culture: every round-1 fix touchpoint carries an in-file comment naming the finding id (data-tables-1/2/5 annotations across supplyChainData, supplyChainResourceIndex, institutionServices, geographyData), making the data layer auditable across review rounds

findings.title: Registry ingest reads IMPORT_GOODS_BY_TIER with the wrong shape — phantom prebuilt goods minted, all real import goods missing
findings.evidence: ingest expects {tier:{goodName:props}} and does `for (const [name, props] of Object.entries(byName))`; IMPORT_GOODS_BY_TIER is {tier:{basic:[...], fromHigher:[...]}} (tradeGoodsData.js:26-121). So `ingest(IMPORT_GOODS_BY_TIER, 'import')` mints goods named 'basic', 'fromHigher', 'fromCityOrMetropolis', 'fromHinterland', 'fromMetropolis' with array props, and no real import good (Salt, Metal tools, Cloth...) is enumerated.
findings.why: listPrebuilt('tradeGoods') feeds EntityPicker and dependency-engine refIds — a user-facing picker shows nonsense entries while the entire import-goods vocabulary is absent from the custom-content dependency system. The bare 'Enslaved persons' key at town (the only shape that ingests correctly) shows the row was authored to fit the broken reader.
findings.fix_shape: Teach ingest the group-array shape (flatten {group:[{name,...}]} entries), delete the anomalous bare town key or move it into a group, and add a joins pin asserting no enumerated prebuilt trade-good name equals a group key and that known import goods appear with direction 'import'.
findings.deferral_checked: Grepped round-1 register, DEAD_CODE_DISPOSITION.md, playbook §0.0.2/0.6 for IMPORT_GOODS/enumeratePrebuilt/fromHigher — no record; fresh finding

subsystems.holistic:
The PDF subsystem is one of the most disciplined surfaces in the codebase, and it visibly got better between rounds. The architecture is exactly right for the product: a single viewModel translation layer (1,309 lines) that owns every shape-coercion the chaotic engine output requires — normSeverity for string/array/min-max severities, coerceProse for object-shaped prose, normalizeIncomeSources reconciling percent-vs-raw so the bar and its label cannot disagree — with each guard annotated with the concrete bug it killed. Sections never reach into raw saves. The live-layer slice (liveWorld.js) genuinely honors its charter of consuming the same pure display selectors the screen uses, and the LIVE_LAYER_FIELDS parity walker is real structural prevention: a future mover that surfaces a read on-screen but forgets the PDF trips a named test instead of silently reopening the round-1 parity gap. The sealed FaithWar chapter is the constitutional showpiece — the three-fold gate (variant+canon, dormant-slice null-collapse, faithUnlocked premium seam) is a pure predicate pinned by an adversarial test that proves the data is present and the gate, not data absence, protects deity names. The 2.99 entitlement chain is fail-closed at every layer I traced: TIER_GATE.free.export=false (the owner-ruled flip landed), canExport → resolveExportAccess decision table → runExport defense-in-depth → server-owned RPC that resolves false on any failure. The F41 worker render lane is mature engineering: keep-alive singleton, id-correlated protocol, feature-detected fallback that refuses to retry real render errors on the main thread, and the nameById plain-data clone seam threaded end-to-end with the hazard documented at both ends.

As simulation substance reaching the eye, the dossier is rich — the round-1 pdf-1 gap (rumors, beliefs, flow drift, pestilence) is closed under the gate discipline, and the campaign PDF gained a State of the Realm chapter that filters concealed sieges and reuses the same read-models. What keeps the slice off a clean A is a residue of legibility-level defects, most of one shape: adapters and copy that drifted from the components they feed. The buyer settlement's trade-war line self-references ('Contesting Iron (Emberhold)' on Emberhold's own paid chapter); the AI arrival scene and pressure sentence are computed into two slices, claimed by a docblock, shown on-screen — and rendered by no chapter; two headline functions receive ad-hoc objects missing the keys their best branches read; the posture/legitimacy bands are copy-paste twins of a Realm helper whose claimed 'mirror' (WarFaithSection) does not exist on this lineage. The ExportSheet's stranded-pick hole shows the pdf-5 fix stopped one step short of the state lifecycle. And four LOW register rows from round 1 (Cover's 'See Summary, page 2' phantom reference chief among them) survived every fix wave — none regressed, none fixed. All are small, none corrupt data, and none breach the constitution: dormancy, byte-identity seams, the premium seam, and the first-paint ratchet (no static @react-pdf import outside the worker graph) all check out. This is production-quality work whose remaining debt is a single afternoon's polish wave plus one product ruling on the dead watermark lane.
strengths: The viewModel single-source-of-truth layer: sections never touch raw saves; every engine-shape hazard (severity arrays, object prose, percent-vs-raw income, object-wrapped scores) is normalized once, with the original bug documented at the fix site — the round-1 finding ids (pdf-1..pdf-6) are breadcrumbed in code, making the register auditable in-file.

The FaithWar three-fold gate is a pure, test-pinned predicate with an adversarial proof that the gate (not data absence) is load-bearing — free/lapsed/anon exports structurally cannot carry a deity name, and the dormant liveWorld slice null-collapses so a peaceful save is byte-identical.

The LIVE_LAYER_FIELDS parity walker (tests/pdf/pdfLiveWorldParity.test.js) is genuine structural prevention: every screen living-world read-model must appear in the PDF slice or a named test fails — the exact machinery that prevents round-1's parity gap from re-opening.

The F41 worker render lane: keep-alive singleton with id-correlated request/response, feature-detected (never UA-sniffed) fallback, DataCloneError demotion, latched-broken state, and the plain-data nameById seam documented at both producer (resolveExportSeam) and consumer (liveWorld).

Print-surface craft rarely seen at this depth: the noLig/ZWNJ ligature-defusal lifecycle including the humanize idempotence trap and uppercase stripZwnj rule; finite/safePct on all bar math; font self-hosting with cache-bust rationale; glyph-safe ASCII connectors in SupplyChainFlow.

The 2.99 entitlement chain is fail-closed end-to-end (client RPC returns false on any failure and the server owns all writes), and the owner-ruled free-export flip is actually enforced in TIER_GATE with the ruling cited.

Test architecture in layers: field-value parity (viewModelParity), golden snapshot (goldenViewModel), render-leaf assertions, and a real end-to-end byte render across variants (fullPdf.render) that pins variant gating by page-count relations.

subsystems.holistic:
This slice is the strongest backend surface I have reviewed at this scale of solo-built product, and it has visibly matured since round 1: of the round-1 backend register, backend-1 (anon checkout rate limiter) is fixed with a documented two-dimension fail-open backstop, the HIGH entity-token half-merge is fixed (the client tokenizer now exists on this lineage at src/lib/entityRefTokenizer.js, consumed by ProseParagraph and the PDF ProseText), ingest-events grew a fail-closed per-actor limiter plus an XFF-resistant per-IP gate and a counted snapshot cap replacing the silent slice(0,2), and both generated _shared bundles are confirmed fresh by recomputing the freshness gate's exact hash.

The money path is the standout. stripe-webhook runs two idempotency belts (a released-on-failure event claim over per-grant atomic claims), the refund/no-refund rule is extracted into a pinned refundPolicy module, and generate-narrative layers a spend-cap reservation (with a written persist-before-release ordering argument), a per-user rate limit, a sufficiency precheck that spares rate-limit units, a free-first-narrative claim with release-on-failure, and a request-idempotency claim whose chargedThisAttempt gate provably prevents a duplicate regen from refunding the prior attempt's spend. Every limiter documents whether it fails open or closed and why; every secret or token compare is constant-time; every anon function is pinned verify_jwt=false deliberately in config.toml with the authenticated set pinned true. Handlers are exported with DI seams so trust boundaries are execution-tested (signature-before-write lexical ordering, XFF-rotation backstop tests). Prompt-injection defense is genuinely layered: fixpoint fence-stripping at every embed site, deterministic server-side entity wrapping that never trusts the model, and an advisory invention signal deliberately quarantined after send({done}) so it can never touch the refund path. The premium seam holds: og-image renders only the sanitized public projection and structurally cannot reach row.data; ingest-events nulls seed below research tier.

What keeps it at A rather than A+: a small set of real defects, mostly at the seams the discipline elsewhere makes conspicuous. The founder clawback violates the file's own documented post-claim failure posture — a transient error after the atomic is_founder flip throws, the redelivery no-ops on the claim, and a refunded founder silently keeps premium and the 30-credit bonus with no remediation row. verify-checkout-session is still the one function on the legacy inline CORS allowlist with an ACAO '*' fallback (round-1 backend-5, known and still open — preview-deploy checkout confirmation breaks there). The shared CORS module's Vercel suffix rule rests on an assumption ("an attacker cannot deploy under our scope") that Vercel's global project-name namespace does not actually guarantee. And the pre-parse body-cap discipline that ingest-events, generate-narrative, and generate-chronicle established has not been swept across the remaining anon-reachable functions. None of these is architectural; all are one-commit fixes.

As product surface, the slice is coherent and complete for its ambition: purchase, fulfillment, clawback, entitlement, recovery, telemetry, ops (pricing resync with guarded parsers and calibration clamps), and abuse defense form a closed system whose failure modes are almost all reasoned about in writing where the next maintainer will read them. The comments are unusually honest — they document why the residual races are accepted and what the operator's remediation surface is. That is what mature production code looks like.
strengths: Money-path idempotency engineering: two-belt webhook dedup (event claim released on handler failure + per-grant atomic claims), refundPolicy extracted as a test-pinned module, spend reservations with a documented persist-before-release ordering rationale, and the chargedThisAttempt crux that makes duplicate regens refund-safe (generate-narrative/index.ts:998-1006)

Every rate limiter and gate documents its fail-open vs fail-closed choice with the threat model (ingest-events fail-closed anonymous sink; create-checkout/verify-single-dossier fail-open to a two-dimension in-memory backstop that defeats XFF rotation; auth-recovery fail-closed with a cumulative per-account lockout and a constant-time verify floor with detached email work)

Constant-time comparison discipline on every secret surface: dossier claim token (account-actions:91), checkout token (verify-single-dossier:17), export shared secret (analytics-export:38), cron secret (pricing-resync-cron:49)
One shared fail-closed CORS module (never '*', dev-gated localhost, Vary handling) adopted by 15 of 16 functions, with per-function verify_jwt pinned explicitly in config.toml and contract-tested
Generated _shared bundles carry a recorded sourceHash enforced by freshness gates — independently CONFIRMED fresh this review by recomputing the exact hash recipe; no hand-edits

Prompt-injection defense in depth: fixpoint fence-stripping re-applied at every embed site (summary, riders, prior prose, guidance), model output never trusted for entity tokens (deterministic parity-tested wrapper), advisory invention signal quarantined off the money path

PII hygiene throughout: peppered device/IP hashes, masked emails with audited full-PII reads (highest role + reason), audit rows that never carry bearer codes, og-image's structural seed-secret firewall
Round-1 remediation actually landed: backend-1 rate limiter, entity-token consumer, ingest-events hardening, founder=30 copy, F4 tier-truth centralization

Unlike the referral clawback, no row records what remains owed.

findings.title: Shared CORS Vercel suffix rule is spoofable: an attacker-named Vercel project's production alias ends with '-settlement-forge.vercel.app'
findings.evidence: `if (url.protocol === 'https:' && url.hostname.endsWith(VERCEL_DEPLOY_SUFFIX)) return true;` — the comment asserts "The team scope is the trailing segment and is owned by us — an attacker cannot deploy under it", but Vercel production aliases are `<project>.vercel.app` in a global first-come namespace: project name `evil-settlement-forge` yields `evil-settlement-forge.vercel.app`, which passes the suffix check.
findings.why: The allowlist's fail-closed invariant (documented as spoof-proof) is falsifiable: a hostile origin gets an exact ACAO echo plus Allow-Credentials:true on every edge function. Practical impact is bounded (auth is bearer-token, not cookie), but the module's central security claim is wrong as written.
findings.fix_shape: Tighten to the deploy-URL shape the comment actually assumes: require the full `<project>-<hash>-settlement-forge.vercel.app` pattern (e.g. /^[a-z0-9-]+-[a-z0-9]{9}-settlement-forge\.vercel\.app$/) or enumerate via ALLOWED_ORIGINS; add a spoof-shaped negative case to cors.test.ts.
findings.deferral_checked: No round-1 entry (the Vercel rule postdates round 1); not in playbook §0.0.2 or any in-file deferral note — the comment claims safety rather than deferring it.

findings.title: Pre-parse body-byte caps are inconsistently applied: five anon-reachable functions buffer unbounded request bodies
findings.evidence: `const { product, checkoutToken, ... } = await req.json();` runs before the rate limiter and the MAX_DOSSIER_BYTES check (which re-serializes post-parse); auth-recovery:261, send-email:359, log-client-error:81 parse unbounded anon bodies; stripe-webhook:909 `await req.text()` buffers before signature rejection. ingest-events/generate-narrative/generate-chronicle all cap bytes pre-parse.
findings.why: The codebase established the byte-cap discipline (and fixed the UTF-16 variant with regression tests) but never swept it across the anon surface; a single oversized POST forces full buffering+parse per request, bounded only by platform limits.
findings.fix_shape: One _shared/readBodyCapped.ts helper (text + byte cap + parse) adopted by all five; caps per function (create-checkout ~600KB to fit the 512KB stash, others 64KB). Mirrors the existing generate-chronicle pattern.

findings.title: checkout.session.async_payment_failed is unhandled — a reserved redeem-code seat leaks permanently on a deferred payment that fails
findings.evidence: The switch handles completed/async_payment_succeeded/expired but `grep async_payment_failed` finds nothing in supabase/functions. Traced: a session that completes with payment_status='unpaid' defers fulfillment; if the async payment then fails, `expired` never fires for a completed session, so revert_redemption never runs.
findings.why: The bound reservation stays 'reserved' forever: that user's once-per-user row is burned and the code's uses_count stays consumed — deferred money leaked with no operator signal. Rare today (card-only checkout), but the redeem lifecycle claims closure.
findings.fix_shape: Add `case 'checkout.session.async_payment_failed':` calling revert_redemption(session.id) — identical body to the expired case; claim-once semantics make it race-safe with a later success.
findings.deferral_checked: No round-1 entry, no in-file seam note (the async_payment_succeeded comment discusses the success leg only); not in playbook ledgers.

findings.title: ingest-events actor first-touch races remain: concurrent device/user link inserts can mint divergent actor ids (round-1 backend-6, still open)
findings.evidence: `await admin.from('analytics_device_links').insert({ device_key: deviceKey, actor_id: actor });` — insert error unchecked, freshly-minted actor returned regardless; resolveUserActor's upsert with ignoreDuplicates:true (line 121) returns its own candidate even when a concurrent writer's row won.
findings.why: Two concurrent first-touch envelopes attribute events to an actor id that never became the durable link — a permanent funnel-stitching blemish in the analytics corpus, invisible at write time.
findings.fix_shape: Upsert with onConflict:'device_key' then re-select the winning actor_id (same for the identity link) — one round-trip more on the cold path only.
findings.deferral_checked: docs/COMPREHENSIVE_REVIEW_2026-07-13.md line 1387: [backend-6] LOW/probable — recorded, verified still present at HEAD; carried at the register's severity.

findings.title: ingest-events swallows insert failures into a 202 and drops event/edit/pulse overflow uncounted — asymmetric with the counted snapshot cap
findings.evidence: `const { error } = await admin.from('analytics_events').upsert(...); if (!error) accepted.events = ...` — on error the response is still 202 with no rejected entry and no log; `body.events.slice(0, 50)` (line 231), edits slice(0,20), pulseEffects slice(0,60) silently discard overflow while snapshots overflow is pushed to `rejected` as 'snapshot_cap_exceeded'.
findings.why: A DB-side failure or an over-batching client loses telemetry invisibly — the exact silent-loss class the SERVER_SNAPSHOT_CAP fix (lib-infra-3) was written to eliminate, still open on the other three planes.
findings.fix_shape: Log insert errors (logError) and count overflow rows into `rejected` with 'event_cap_exceeded'-style reasons, mirroring the snapshot treatment; optionally surface accepted<sent to the client queue for re-spill.
findings.deferral_checked: Round-1 fixed only the snapshot plane (lib-infra-3); no recorded decision covering events/edits/pulse overflow or insert-error swallowing.

findings.title: invoice.paid with no matching profile throws forever — a manually-created Stripe customer's invoice retry-loops through the webhook (round-1 nit, still open)
findings.evidence: `throw new Error(`Monthly allowance invoice ${invoice.id} has no matching profile`)` — the throw releases the event claim, Stripe redelivers on its full backoff schedule, and every delivery re-throws until Stripe abandons (~3 days of noise per invoice).
findings.why: Operator-created or migrated Stripe customers with no profiles row turn into multi-day webhook-failure noise that masks real failures in the dashboard; nothing is fulfillable, so the retries buy nothing.
findings.fix_shape: Ack unmatched non-subscription-linked invoices with a structured logError breadcrumb instead of throwing, or throw only when a customerId exists but the email fallback also matched nothing after a bounded retry count.
findings.deferral_checked: Recorded in the round-1 nit batch (register line ~1396, item 2); verified still present at HEAD — carried forward at low, matching the register.

findings.title: admin get_stats selects every profiles row unbounded — silently wrong stats past PostgREST's max-rows and a growing full-table read
findings.evidence: `const { data: profiles } = await adminClient.from('profiles').select('tier, role, credits');` then JS-side count/reduce over the returned rows — no .limit, no aggregate; PostgREST caps the response (default 1000 rows), after which total/premiumCount/totalCredits undercount without any error.
findings.why: The admin dashboard's headline numbers silently freeze at the row cap as the user base grows — a wrong-number bug that looks like a plateau, on the surface an operator trusts for business decisions.
findings.fix_shape: Replace with one SECURITY DEFINER admin_stats() RPC doing count(*)/sum(credits) grouped by tier/role — same pattern as the existing report_* functions this file already dispatches to.
findings.deferral_checked: Not in the round-1 register (admin-actions entries covered PII redaction and role gates), no in-file note; checked playbook §0.6 rulings — absent.

findings.title: create-checkout ignores the profiles read error from .single() — a profile-less authed user mints a fresh orphan Stripe customer on every checkout
findings.evidence: `const { data: profile } = await admin.from('profiles').select('stripe_customer_id').eq('id', user.id).single();` — .single() errors on zero rows, the error is never destructured, profile is undefined, so a new Stripe customer is created and the follow-up `.update(...).eq('id', user.id)` writes zero rows silently.
findings.why: Any user whose profiles row is missing (failed trigger, migration gap) accumulates one orphan Stripe customer per checkout and never gets a durable stripe_customer_id binding — the webhook's email-fallback then carries the whole matching burden for money events.
findings.fix_shape: Use .maybeSingle(), check the error, and upsert the profiles binding (or fail loud into the generic 400) — mirrors create-customer-portal's identity-match care on the same read.
findings.deferral_checked: No round-1 entry or in-file note; the sibling create-customer-portal read at line 72 already uses .maybeSingle(), confirming the intended idiom.

findings.title: Privilege-mutation RPC service_update_profile_metadata retains the default PUBLIC execute grant (no revoke-from-public)
findings.evidence: Statement-level census across all 134 migrations: the ONLY grant/revoke touching this function is `grant execute on function public.service_update_profile_metadata(uuid, uuid, jsonb, text) to service_role;` (017:366). No migration (incl. 062 'close_authz_gaps', which only drops a policy + enables RLS on 2 tables) ever REVOKEs the inherited PUBLIC grant. Its sibling service_set_credits got exactly this fix in 113.
findings.why: This RPC sets role/tier/is_founder — a privilege-escalation-shaped surface, and 062 GAP-2 explicitly designates it one of the trusted audited write paths after removing the direct profiles-UPDATE bypass. It retains the CREATE-time default PUBLIC execute, so it is callable by any anon/authenticated caller over PostgREST. Not a live hole: the body's first statement `perform public._assert_service_admin_actor(actor_user)` raises unless the JWT role is service_role AND the actor is developer/admin (fail-closed) — the same defense-in-depth gap 113 named for service_set_credits.
findings.fix_shape: A grant-only migration mirroring 113: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.service_update_profile_metadata(uuid,uuid,jsonb,text) FROM public, anon, authenticated; then re-GRANT EXECUTE to service_role. Better: add a structural ratchet (like migrationSearchPathPin) asserting every SECURITY DEFINER money/privilege RPC is revoked from PUBLIC — the absence of such a guard is why this slipped when 113 fixed only one sibling.
findings.deferral_checked: Checked round-1 backend-3 (search_path, unrelated) and backend-1 (create-checkout rate limit); the 113 migration comment names service_adjust_credits + get_credit_balance as the locked siblings but NOT service_update_profile_metadata; no deferral ledger (playbook 0.0.2/0.6/0.8, DEAD_CODE_DISPOSITION) records this grant gap.

findings.title: search_path ratchet baseline can mask a LIVE pin regression when a baselined pre-094 function is recreated with a bare header
findings.evidence: The walker reads search_path from each function's net-current `create or replace` HEADER and is 'blind to ALTER' (its own comment, lines 28-31). 094 pinned the 74 pre-094 definers via an ALTER DO-block; their net-current headers stay bare `set search_path = public` (frozen in the 76-entry baseline). The 'adds no NEW' check only flags names absent from the baseline; the 'no stale' check only flags baselined names that became non-bare.
findings.why: A future migration that recreates any baselined pre-094 function (e.g. get_credit_balance/system_grant_credits) with the historical bare `set search_path = public` header resets its LIVE proconfig to bare public (create-or-replace overwrites proconfig; 094's DO-block never re-runs), reinstating the CVE-2018-1058 pg_temp-first posture — while the ratchet stays green (the name is still bare AND still baselined: neither 'added' nor 'stale'). The guard catches new bare definers and re-pins, but not regressions of already-baselined ones.
findings.fix_shape: Have the ratchet resolve the EFFECTIVE pin the way the DB will (treat a baselined function as pinned only if its net-current recreate is <=094 OR its header pins pg_temp), or add a rule that any migration recreating a baselined function must pin `public, pg_temp` in the new header (131's pattern). Low-risk class on Supabase per 094's own note, but the structural-prevention intent is currently defeatable.
findings.deferral_checked: Checked round-1 backend-3 (resolved by 131 + this ratchet) and the ratchet's own header comments — they acknowledge ALTER-blindness for the 103 service_* baseline entries but do NOT acknowledge the recreate-regression direction; no deferral ledger records it.

subsystems.holistic:
This slice is the most hardened surface I have seen in a solo-built repo, and — unusually — its quality is load-bearing rather than decorative: in a project whose constitution is enforced by ratchets, the gate machinery IS the constitution. The round-1 highs in this slice were genuinely fixed, not papered over. VERIFY_DIST now has an unconditional hard-fail sentinel (vendorPdfLazy.test.js:407) so the first-paint budget can never again count green on a missing dist; check-domain-strict gained a broken-toolchain anti-vacuity sentinel that distinguishes "ran clean" from "did not run"; the Vercel ignoreCommand gate is a small masterpiece of fail-closed thinking — it inverts correctly around Vercel's exit-code convention, catches its own crashes (a thrown error would otherwise read as PROCEED), blocks token-less and metadata-less CLI prod deploys, dedupes re-run check names with success-wins logic, and layers a migration-currency gate on top, with every branch pinned by ciGateHardening.test.js and the REQUIRED_CHECKS list drift-guarded against ci.yml job names in both directions. The local/CI parity test, the e2e anti-vacuity guard (static discovery + runtime executed-count), the mutation sweep with its dirty-tree refusal, the five shrink-only baselines each verified to have an enforcing consumer, and the derived-not-curated chunk-split machinery in vite.config.js (engine-shared closure, eager module graph, icon and data splits — each with a documented fail-safe direction and a named enforcing test) together form a coherent anti-vacuity doctrine that the repo demonstrably applies to itself recursively: gates that verify gates, and a weekly sweep that plants regressions to prove the gates catch them.

The findings are correspondingly narrow, and the two that matter share one shape: the enforcement spine lagging an architecture move. The data-purity fence (lint rule + source-regex twin + mutation-sweep plant) still points at src/generators/rngContext.js, but the RNG seam moved to src/kernel/ — the one bug class the fence exists to stop is now importable around it, and the weekly sweep certifies the stale fence. Second, the stale-dist problem was fixed in the vacuity direction (verify:dist post-build) but not the false-red direction: check still executes the dist-reading contracts before build against the previous dist, a recurring operational tax the repo has already invented the cure for (the VERIFY_DIST skipIf idiom) and applied to exactly one assertion. Third, the soak surface has outgrown its CI lane: whole-world-soak is a real pass/fail watchdog — same-seed byte-identity at the composed-kernel level plus a cost envelope — that runs nowhere on a schedule, while the lane still runs only the religion-era probes under a now-stale "diagnostic-only" rationale.

As product surface, this slice mostly serves the operator, and it serves them well: error messages name the remediation command, the deploy gate's skip reasons explain the redeploy loop, and the generated artifacts (glossary, analytics dictionary, sitemap) are freshness-pinned so the user-facing references cannot drift from code. The audit soaks are simulation-substance instruments of real quality — deterministic, tuned-nothing, panel-structured evidence generators that read like lab notebooks. Residual weaknesses are honest and recorded: CSP remains Report-Only (adjudicated deferral), e2e runs against the dev server rather than the built bundle, e2e/ and api/ sit outside lint, and a handful of round-1 comment-drift nits persist untouched in the enforcement layer where comments are operator guidance. Grade A: the slice's core duties — single-point budget enforcement, fail-closed deploys, CI/local parity — are airtight; the deductions are two medium-grade fence-lag gaps and hygiene debt.
strengths: Fail-closed deploy gate done right: vercel-ignore-build.mjs handles the exit-code inversion, crash-as-proceed, token-less and CLI-metadata-less deploys, re-run dedup (success-wins + filter=latest), and migration-currency drift — every branch exercised by ciGateHardening.test.js against the real decideDeploy(), with REQUIRED_CHECKS ⇔ ci.yml job names pinned both directions and mirrored by the deploy job's needs list

A recursive anti-vacuity doctrine: VERIFY_DIST unconditional hard-fail sentinel, check-domain-strict's broken-toolchain sentinel, e2e static+runtime executed-count guards, ciCheckParity's bidirectional local/CI step parity, and a weekly mutation sweep that plants regressions to prove the spine holds — gates that verify gates

Derived-not-curated build splits in vite.config.js (engine-shared domain closure, chunk-level eager module graph, icon and data splits) where every rule documents its fail-safe direction and names its enforcing test; the budget itself is single-point (tests/build/vendorPdfLazy.test.js) and reached only through verify:dist post-build

Ratchet discipline is uniform and consumer-verified: all five scripts/.​*-baseline.json files have enforcing tests/plugins; baselines are shrink-only with explicit re-baseline commands and never-widen doctrine in every error message

Generated artifacts (sitemap, glossary, analytics dictionary, edge bundles) are all freshness-pinned byte-identical against fresh generation, with the edge-bundle sourceHash covering the full transitive input set via the esbuild metafile

The audit soaks are high-grade simulation instruments — deterministic, seeded, tune-nothing, panel-structured (whole-world-soak asserts composed-engine same-seed byte-identity, seed divergence, population bounds, and a serialized-bytes cost envelope with documented equilibrium findings)

findings.title: layerBoundaries cycle baseline can silently miss a NEW cycle that threads through an already-finished node — enforcement depends on lexicographic DFS order
findings.evidence: `if (s === 1) cycles.add(canonical(stack.slice(stack.indexOf(next)))); else if (s === 0) dfs(next);` — a neighbor in state 2 (done) is ignored. Traced: with allowed cycle helpers>priorityHelpers, adding helpers→newMod→priorityHelpers is recorded ONLY if 'newMod' sorts before 'priorityHelpers'; otherwise priorityHelpers finishes first, newMod→priorityHelpers is a cross edge, and the new 3-cycle is never enumerated — gate stays green.
findings.why: This is the shrink-only architecture ratchet ('adding one → this fails'). The hole clusters exactly around the two ALLOWED cycles' members — helpers.js/priorityHelpers.js are hub generator modules where a new cycle is most likely to form — and whether it is caught depends on file naming, not structure.
findings.fix_shape: Replace back-edge enumeration with SCC comparison (Tarjan, ~30 lines): assert every strongly-connected component is a singleton OR exactly equals an allowed cycle's member set. SCCs are traversal-order-invariant, so the baseline becomes airtight instead of name-dependent. Also delete the dead `existsSync(base) ? null : null` at :112.

subsystems.holistic:
This test estate is the strongest artifact in the repository and, frankly, stronger than most professional codebases I have reviewed at any scale. Its defining property is that the guards guard the guards: the first-paint ratchet (vendorPdfLazy) carries not just a monotone byte budget but a full decision archaeology of every raise and reclaim, an unconditional VERIFY_DIST anti-vacuity test that cannot itself be vacated, and sentinel PRESENCE checks that prove the lazy-leaf ABSENCE checks are non-vacuous. The e2e layer has a forged-Playwright-JSON test of the script that detects all-skipped green runs. The enforcement-claims meta-pin makes prose like 'promoted to ERROR' gate-checked. ciCheckParity and ciGateHardening pin local↔CI parity and fail-closed deploy decisions by exercising real decision functions, not string presence. This is structural-prevention culture fully institutionalized.

Coverage shape against the new kernels is complete on the house pattern: every one of the ~7 new movers (upswing, resourceDynamics, convergence, momentum, settlement lifecycle, naval, peace-causal) ships a unit suite, a fenced pre-wire dormancy golden with a lit-path anti-vacuity twin, and manifest/walker registration checks. The realmCoverage walker deserves special mention — it source-scans worldPulse for forceable shapes and fail-closes the Counterpart Criterion with a shrink-only PARKED ledger at zero, which is the constitution turned into a test. Golden hygiene is verifiable in git: dormancy manifests were captured once, pre-wire, and never re-minted; the generator golden master's regens are all owner-signed commits. Round-1's top findings (VERIFY_DIST vacuity, stale-graph goldens, pglite skip-vacuity, self-minting manifests, catch-up persist round-trip, the everything-on composition gap, the pipeline flake) were all fixed with finding IDs cited in-file — remediation traceability most teams never achieve.

The weaknesses are real but peripheral. The e2e layer remains the thinnest stratum: 8 specs, two of which still contain the round-1-flagged assertion-free bodies, and no e2e touches the composer/docket/realm surfaces at all — the browser-level trust chain leans on the anti-vacuity ratchet plus jsdom smokes. Component-level coverage of the newest legibility surfaces (RealmDocket, RealmForecast, the WorldPulsePanel catch-up trigger) is module-eval-only while their store/domain layers are excellent — an inversion of risk, since the wiring seam is where these break. Two structural debts sit in the substrate: the dormancy oracle lives inside a test file imported by 21 suites (registration duplication plus rename fragility on the constitution's measuring stick), and the architecture cycle baseline's DFS enumeration is traversal-order-dependent, so a new cycle threading the existing helpers/priorityHelpers cycle can pass silently. Money-path coverage floors remain honest but thin (stripe.js floored at 0) — recorded round-1 and unchanged. Dormancy golden corpora are deliberately short-horizon (3 configs, 4–8 ticks); they prove no-write-on-load and short-run byte identity, while long-horizon drift is delegated to the soaks, which is a reasonable documented trade.

As product surface, the estate directly encodes the constitution: byte-identity, dormancy, the premium seam (28 security suites incl. pglite execution against real SQL), the ratchet, and the counterpart criterion each have named enforcement. Grade A rather than A+ because the browser-level layer and the newest UI seams lag the engine's rigor, and two substrate defects sit in constitutional gates themselves.

findings.title: upswingKernel freshSettlement reads the stale pre-clone updates array — same-tick cross-arc writes clobber each other and can re-arm a completed reconstruction
findings.evidence: `const freshSettlement = (id) => { const ui = updateIndex.get(String(id)); if (ui !== undefined) return updates[ui]?.settlement; ... }` — reads the ORIGINAL `updates` array, while all writes go to `nextUpdates` after ensureCloned(). The sibling settlementLifecycleKernel.js:471 correctly reads `nextUpdates[ui]?.settlement`.
findings.why: The B2 boom/bust pass (line 570, 594) and B3 flourishing pass (line 664, 677, 698) re-fetch via freshSettlement and then REPLACE nextUpdates[ui].settlement wholesale. If the same settlement was written by an earlier pass the same tick (recon condition mint, recon completion: reconstructedAt stamps + institution upgrade + history beat + skim), those writes are silently lost. Losing the reconstructedAt stamps lets recentUnreconstructedCalamity re-arm the SAME calamity within its 3-year window — a repeated legitimacy dividend/upgrade from one source, violating the kernel's own 'conservation absolute' header. Deterministic, but incoherent composition in a constitutional kernel.
findings.fix_shape: Change freshSettlement to read nextUpdates (the lifecycle-kernel idiom) — one-word fix; add a same-tick composition pin (recon-completes + boom-busts same tick; boom-mints + flourish-mints same tick) proving no write is lost. Consider extracting the shared freshSettlement/ensureCloned helper so the two kernels cannot diverge again.

dimensions.holistic:
This dimension is the constitution's home turf, and the codebase honors it with unusual rigor. The randomness architecture is genuinely fail-closed: rngContext throws in every environment when a draw happens outside a seeded scope, the sole escape hatch is a deliberately greppable named function, and the eslint fence bans Math.random, no-arg Date construction, Date.now, localeCompare, all toLocale* formatters, and Intl across src/generators, src/domain, and src/workers with per-tree explanatory messages — each backed by a source-regex guard test (domainWallClock, localeCompareGuard, localeFormatGuard) so skipping lint does not skip the law. The wall clock has exactly one sanctioned domain read (clock.js), and assertNowPinnedInTest converts the pin-now convention into a structural guard at both pulse entry points.

The loaded-dice law is not aspirational — it is implemented. The tick PRNG reseeds from `${rngSeed}::tick:N::interval`; the 70-site fork census across worldPulse shows stable keys nearly everywhere (per-candidate roll keys, order-symmetric battle keys sorted before joining, per-parent-per-tick satellite forks with draws consumed in codepoint order). Selection loops that precede a draw sort by codepoint with explicit tiebreaks; momentum's fold is deliberately permutation-independent; the frozen spatial digest builder documents and implements a provably deterministic Dijkstra with explicit heap tie-breaks, and no live mover writes into spatialDigest — everything mutable lives in spatialLedgers.

The dormancy audit of the five new kernels comes back clean at the gate level: upswingArcsEnabled, resourceDynamicsEnabled, settlementLifecycleEnabled, momentumEnabled, and interventionEnabled are all virtual (absent from DEFAULT_SIMULATION_RULES, preserved untouched through normalizeSimulationRules' input spread, fail-closed on garbage), all gates early-return with the same reference, ledgers drop-when-empty, and every kernel has a fenced dormancy golden in tests/property. The normalizer itself is a small masterclass: boolean keys coerce fail-closed, profile keys stay virtual until touched, and preset identity survives axis unlocks by design.

The blemish is inside the newest constitutional kernel. upswingKernel's freshSettlement closure reads the pre-clone updates array where its sibling lifecycle kernel correctly reads nextUpdates — so the kernel's three sequential arc passes (reconstruction, boom/bust, flourishing) can silently clobber one another's same-tick writes to the same settlement, and losing the reconstructedAt stamps can re-arm a completed rebuild, breaking the kernel's own conservation pledge. It is deterministic (same wrong bytes every run), so Law 1 survives, but it is exactly the composition-incoherence class this review hunts, it is untested (no same-tick composition pin), and it sits in the layer the endgame plans to light. The remaining findings are contract-legibility drift: a header advertising forks that do not exist, an escape hatch nothing adopted, cooldown stamps whose names overstate their semantics.

As product surface, determinism here is not just correctness plumbing — it is what makes the forecast (preview≡apply), the pause/dismiss equivalence invariant, and the catch-up collapse trustworthy, and those invariants are machine-enforced (residue-strip registry, byte-identity tests) rather than prose. Graded as mature production code for this ambition, the determinism constitution is the strongest subsystem I have reviewed in this codebase: one real high-severity composition bug in a dark-by-default kernel keeps it from a clean A.
strengths: Fail-closed rngContext: ambient draws THROW in every environment (test/dev/prod), with a single named, greppable escape hatch and a save/restore stack for nested generation — silent seed-divergence is structurally impossible in the fenced trees

The eslint determinism fence (Math.random / Date.now / new Date() / localeCompare / toLocale* / Intl banned in src/generators + src/domain + src/workers with per-rule teaching messages) is backed by source-regex guard tests so the law survives a skipped lint

Loaded-dice discipline is real: per-tick reseeded parent PRNG + 70 audited fork sites on stable keys (order-symmetric battle keys, per-candidate roll keys, per-parent satellite forks with fixed draw order), codepoint sorts before every selection loop, permutation-independent ledger folds (momentum)

Dormancy constitution fully honored by all five new kernels: virtual flags absent from DEFAULT_SIMULATION_RULES, same-reference early returns, drop-when-empty ledgers, and a fenced byte-identity dormancy golden per kernel (tests/property/*DormancyGolden)

The frozen spatial digest is a keystone done right: provably deterministic multi-source Dijkstra with explicit tie-breaks documented AND implemented, versioned re-canonize axes, and zero live-mover writes into the digest (census-verified)
wallClockNow is one seam with a structural test-time pin guard (assertNowPinnedInTest) at both pulse entry points; every domain timestamp threads caller-pinned now
normalizeSimulationRules fail-closes malformed booleans, keeps profile keys virtual-until-touched, and preserves unknown virtual flags untouched — the write-on-load class has no habitat
